nodes.title: Normalized coefficient datum
nodes.statement: A normalized datum consists of p prime, s≥1, k=F_q with q=p^s, a complete mixed-characteristic DVR R with residue k, K=Frac(R), a chosen square root c_p of p in K and c_q=c_p^s, a nontrivial additive character ψ of F_p and its compatible Dwork parameter π with π^(p−1)=−p. Coefficients may be enlarged finitely. Use ψ∘Tr_{k_d/F_p} over k_d, half twists with q-Frobenius scalar c_q^(−1), and v(q)=1. For degree d, the normalized rank-r scalar trace is (−1)^(r−1)c_q^(−d(r−1)) times the raw sum over k_d. A point valued in k_d of smaller degree uses repeated Frobenius, rather than a shorter product.
hypotheses: Use the normalized datum of KB.0: split pinned G, dual H, X=G_m over k=F_q, K containing π and the chosen square root of p. Group-valued monodromy assertions assume H almost simple unless their statement explicitly takes products or a torus. All further rank, prime and character restrictions are stated in the target.
proofSteps: Import the existing additive-character and finite-field trace operations and the scalar normalized sheaf.
Adjoin π and c_p simultaneously, fix their choices and extend scalars through all coefficient categories.
Check degrees and half twists before comparing trace functions.

nodes.title: Exponential and Kummer sign dictionary
nodes.statement: For column-vector connections and a horizontal Frobenius map F* M→M, the Dwork object with multiplier exp(π(t−t^p)) has connection d−πdt. Write E_λ=(O,d+λdt); then E_{−π} is its algebraic precursor. For a Kummer connection d−a dx/x with (q−1)a integral, the horizontal q-Frobenius multiplier is x^{−(q−1)a}; it realizes the inverse of the Teichmüller character x↦x^{(q−1)a}. To realize that character use the opposite exponent. Algebraic integer exponents alone cannot encode a nontrivial tame finite-field character in the de Rham–rigid comparison.
hypotheses: Use the normalized datum of KB.0: split pinned G, dual H, X=G_m over k=F_q, K containing π and the chosen square root of p. Group-valued monodromy assertions assume H almost simple unless their statement explicitly takes products or a torus. All further rank, prime and character restrictions are stated in the target.
Frobenius is taken relative to the displayed lift and constant coefficient automorphism; use the iterated p-Frobenius for q.
proofSteps: Differentiate the multipliers and use C′+A C=C A_F for the column connection.
Evaluate the Kummer multiplier on Teichmüller units and compare the character.

Take the dual of the existing all-prime Dwork object with connection d+πdt to obtain E_{−π}; the RD.1 local example by itself assumes p odd. Match rational Kummer exponents modulo integers rather than differentiating an algebraic character.

nodes.title: Affine generic level quotient
nodes.statement: For split pinned G and the alcove determined by B⊃T at ∞, let I₀ be the Iwahori and I₁ its pro-unipotent radical. Define I₂ by the root-depth filtration: it contains T(1) and all nonsimple positive affine-root groups. Then V=I₁/I₂ is the direct sum of the affine-simple root lines of the derived root system. A linear functional φ:V→G_a is generic when each such coordinate is nonzero; over R require nonzero reduction in every line. For a torus V=0. Do not replace I₂ by the product of the congruence center and the commutator subgroup in residue characteristics dividing an isogeny degree.
hypotheses: Use the normalized datum of KB.0: split pinned G, dual H, X=G_m over k=F_q, K containing π and the chosen square root of p. Group-valued monodromy assertions assume H almost simple unless their statement explicitly takes products or a torus. All further rank, prime and character restrictions are stated in the target.
proofSteps: Take the root-group level filtration on the pinned split group scheme.
Project to affine-simple root coordinates; verify the kernel includes the toral congruence subgroup.
Define genericity as the complement of the union of coordinate hyperplanes.

nodes.title: Clean automorphic datum
nodes.statement: For generic φ on V, define A on the γ component of Bun_G(0,2) as the shifted extension of φ*AS_ψ along j_γ, with the shift prescribed by the holonomic heart. Restriction to the base point induces an equivalence from (V,φ*AS_ψ)-equivariant holonomic objects on that component to coefficient objects on a point. Construct the analogous exponential de Rham and arithmetic D-module objects with their own coefficient conventions.

nodes.title: Kloosterman Hecke eigenobject
nodes.statement: There is an exact tensor functor Kl_H^rig(ψφ):Rep(H)→F-Isoc†(X/K) and a Hecke eigenisomorphism Hk_W(A)≅A⊠Kl_W, compatible with fusion and all intertwiners. nodes.title: Tame-character eigenobject
nodes.statement: For a character χ:T(k)→K× and a splitting s:T⋊Ω≅T̃, use on the γ chart K_{χγ}⊠φ*AS_ψ, with χγ=χ∘Adγ. nodes.title: Frenkel–Gross connection
nodes.statement: Let H be split reductive in characteristic zero with a fixed pinning. Put N=Σ simple-root vectors, and choose a nonzero lowest-root vector E_i in each simple derived factor. The H-connection on the trivial bundle over X is ∇=d+(N+xΣE_i)dx/x, interpreted through every algebraic representation as a tensor functor. For the parameter λ use A_λ=N+xΣλ^{h_i}E_i, with the Coxeter number h_i of that factor. The torus factor has zero connection. Pinning changes act by gauge transformations and coordinate rescaling; a single common exponent is not used for unequal factors.

The normalized identities are obtained by division by Q^n. In odd characteristic g here is the Gauss sum for the field F_Q; extension from a fixed base field must use Hasse–Davenport consistently.

nodes.title: Toric hypergeometric slopes
nodes.statement: For odd p, n≥1, d|p−1 and a≠0, let f_d=Σ_{i=1}^{2n}x_i−z^d+a z^d/(∏_{i=1}^{2n}x_i) on G_m^{2n+1}. It is nondegenerate; its Newton polytope has dimension 2n+1 and volume d/(2n)!, and its L-polynomial has degree d(2n+1). Its Hodge and Newton slopes are j/d for 0≤j<d(2n+1), each once. For d=1,2 the exact identity S_m(f₂)−S_m(f₁)=H_{ψ,m}(2n+1;ρ)(a) equals minus the trace of the unnormalized hypergeometric object. Dividing L-polynomials therefore leaves the unnormalized hypergeometric slopes 1/2,3/2,…,2n+1/2 at every a.
